While the 	ext{live-wip-2026-09-24} branch contains a diagnostic tool that prints the key mode, it lacks a hard assertion. This asymmetry creates a silent failure mode: a test key in production yields a "green" report indicating "LIVE mode", which operator reads past without intervention. Mathematically, we can model this as a binary classification problem where the true label T \in \{	ext{LIVE}, 	ext{TEST}\} and the observed label O \in \{	ext{LIVE}, 	ext{TEST}\}. The audit shows that P(O = 	ext{LIVE} | T = 	ext{TEST}) > 0, leading to undetected misconfigurations. To mitigate this, we introduce a threshold-based verifier V(k) = \mathbb{I}[\mathcal{M}(k) = E] - \epsilon, where \epsilon controls false positives. Empirically, we observe that \mathbb{E}[V(k)] decreases as the proportion of test keys in prod increases, providing a concrete metric for remediation.
